# enforcement-seams.tsv — the POSTURE census behind the public "deny-closed enforcement
# points" claim (README family x7, org profile, docs-site, launch material).
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until 2026-08-05 both counters measured the EXISTENCE OF A FILE:
#   ai-state.sh          for f in <paths>; do [ -f "$f" ] && echo x; done | wc -l
#   check-public-counts  enforcement = sum(1 for f in seams if os.path.isfile(f))
# A seam file present but fail-OPEN counted exactly the same as a deny-closed one, so the
# published adjective "deny-closed" rested on nothing the gate could see. That the number
# was right was a coincidence, not a measurement — and the audit that replaced it found
# TWO of the four paths were not even the enforcement point:
#   modules/inferenceproxy/api.go   is the module's ADMIN CRUD surface. Its own package
#                                   doc says so: "This module DECIDES NOTHING about a
#                                   live request" (modules/inferenceproxy/doc.go:13).
#                                   The governed decider is cmd/olivares/inferenceproxy.go.
#   connectors/a2a/a2a.go           is the read-only Agent-Card SourceConnector. It holds
#                                   no gate at all; the delegation PEP is connectors/a2a/pep.go.
# A seam now counts only when a test PROVES it denies in the absence of an allow. The
# proof must live inside the named test function, between its declaration and a closing
# brace at column 0, AND inside a failing call (t.Fatal/t.Error): a file that merely
# mentions the string is not a proof, a function gutted to a no-op stops counting even if
# its name stays, and a t.Log or a comment carrying the same words is text that looks like
# enforcement. A duplicated seam, proof or label is refused outright — one enforcement
# point is one row, or three real seams could publish "four" by listing one of them twice.
# Both counters read THIS file and agree on what a valid row is, so the two cannot drift.
# WHAT THIS CENSUS DOES NOT PROVE, said plainly so nobody has to discover it. It checks
# that the proof is THERE, not that it PASSES: neither counter compiles or runs Go, because
# both must work in the curated public export and in a fast branch lint that deliberately
# builds nothing. A proof whose assertion is intact but whose product code regressed is
# caught by `task test` and by mainline-ci, not here. So this number means "four seams
# still carry an intact deny-by-default proof", which is strictly more than the file-
# existence check it replaced and strictly less than "four seams are green right now".
# Closing that last gap means running the named tests from the counter — a real change of
# what lint:public-counts is, and an owner's call, not a session's.
# DENY-BY-DEFAULT, precisely: the test drives an ABSENT / UNCONFIGURED / UNREADABLE path
# — no gate wired, an empty policy document, a store that will not answer — and asserts a
# refusal. A test proving "an explicit deny rule denies" does NOT qualify and must not be
# listed here; it proves the engine works, not that silence is safe.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   1 seam_file    the product file where the deny-closed fallback actually lives
#   2 test_file    the file holding the proof
#   3 test_func    ERE matching the proof function's declaration line
#   4 assertion    ERE that must appear INSIDE that function's body
#   5 label        what the public copy calls this enforcement point
# Adding a row raises the published count and every public surface must be updated with
# it; the gate will say so. Removing a proof lowers it and turns lint:public-counts RED —
# verified by mutation in both directions on 2026-08-05, not merely observed green.
cmd/olivares/claudehookpep.go
cmd/olivares/inferenceproxy.go
connectors/mcp/gate.go
